title: Modular runbook cards + progressive upgrade strip for Private/VPC first-run
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a compact, modular runbook card set and a progressive upgrade UI strip for the Private/VPC first-run experience. Goal is to reduce cognitive load during operator setup by surfacing lightweight, actionable cards (Network verification, Credentials, KMS, Health-checks, Rollback) and a persistent, non-blocking upgrade strip that surfaces critical upgrade actions and status without breaking the runflow. Deliverables: Figma kit (cards + states), Hi-fi screenshots for release notes, accessible microcopy, SVG icon set, and annotated handoff spec for engineering.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma file with all card variants (idle, in-progress, success, error, retry) reviewed and approved by PM and Eng; 2) Upgrade strip prototypes demonstrating progressive disclosure and rollback CTA; 3) Exported PNG/SVG mockups for release notes and inline console screenshots; 4) Accessibility check (contrast, keyboard focus) documented; 5) Handoff doc with tokenized spacing and component props attached to the PRD.
deliverables: Figma: Modular Runbook Card Library (pages: Tokens, Components, Examples)
Figma: Progressive Upgrade Strip prototype (responsive frames)
Screenshot exports: 3 sizes (desktop/tablet/compact) in Drive folder
steps: Kickoff alignment with PM/Eng -> confirmed scope and constraints
Chosen direction: modular runbook cards + non-blocking upgrade strip
Create Figma tokens and component variants
Iterate hi-fi mockups with accessibility adjustments
Export screenshot set and write handoff spec
Design review and sign-off, then attach to GH PR for implementation
comments: 2025-10-03 - Aisha: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma. Direction A (compact stacked cards) and C (horizontal strip) look promising; leaning toward hybrid.
2025-10-06 - Carlos (Eng): Confirmed feasibility for animated progress states; ask to keep mount cost minimal (no heavy JS for simple states).
2025-10-08 - Lena (PM): Requested explicit KMS card and a soft rollback CTA when upgrade fails; prioritize microcopy for security warnings.
2025-10-10 - Marco (Design lead): Iteration 2 uploaded. Adjusted button hierarchy and contrast for WCAG AA. Need engineering to confirm token names for spacing.
2025-10-12 - Sana (Security): Reviewed copy; suggested replacing 'Force upgrade' with 'Retry upgrade with migration plan' wording to reduce operator risk.

2025-10-14 - Aisha: Prepared screenshot exports and created handoff doc. Ready for Eng handoff and A11y pass. Noted one edge-case: intermittent NAT failure visual state that requires error affordance.

2025-10-15 - Carlos (Eng): Spot review done; PR #8421 opened referencing this design. Two follow-ups: 1) add a collapsed card state for telemetry-limited installs; 2) confirm retry-backoff animation timing.
implementation_notes: Prefer CSS transitions for progress states; avoid heavy animation libraries.
Card props: id, title, description, status(enum), primary_cta, secondary_cta, details_url.
Upgrade strip should be sticky but non-modal; allow auto-collapse after success or manual dismiss with persisted preference per operator.
Telemetry-limited installs: show collapsed card with a single 'Run checks' action that expands on click.
Failure state: include one-line remediation hint + link to runbook details in Confluence.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overloading run flow with too many cards -> Mitigation: prioritize 4 core cards and provide 'More' expansion.
Risk: Upgrade strip perceived as modal -> Mitigation: make it visually subdued, left-aligned icon, secondary color, and add clear dismiss behavior.
Risk: Accessibility issues for compact screenshots -> Mitigation: test with keyboard-only and color-contrast tool; increase hit target sizes.
qa_checklist: All card states render correctly at 320/768/1440 widths
Keyboard navigation order is logical and focus ring present
Color contrast meets WCAG AA for text and critical icons
Upgrade strip dismiss preference persists after reload
Error states include actionable remediation link to Confluence
notes: This ticket focuses strictly on visual assets and handoff; implementation of the runtime checks and backend signals are tracked in ENG-31254. Avoid scope creep into new metrics telemetry work; that will be a follow-up once the UI is stable.
